name: Kapferer’s Brand Identity Prism
diagnostic: How do our external physical codes and relational behaviors mirror the internal culture of our organization and the aspirational self-image of our buyer?
artifact: A six-facet identity prism: Physique, Personality, Culture, Relationship, Reflection, Self-Image.
trap: An identity built entirely on Reflection: customer-pandering marketing with no operational or cultural grounding.
pedigreeFull: Jean-Noël Kapferer (*Strategic Brand Management*, 1992). An academic formulation asserting that a brand exists as a hexagonal prism balanced along externalization-internalization and sender-receiver axes.
artifactFull: A Hexagonal Identity Prism Matrix articulating six structural facets: Physique (visual and physical cues), Personality (character profile), Culture (ideological values), Relationship (mode of interaction), Reflection (perceived target customer), and Self-Image (the customer's internal identity affirmation).
trapFull: Constructing an identity focused entirely on "Reflection," creating customer-pandering marketing that lacks internal operational or cultural grounding.
